strings.name: Meg O’Neill
strings.summary: O’Neill moved from engineering into international oil and gas operations. After ExxonMobil she joined Woodside, became acting and then permanent CEO, and led its merger with BHP’s petroleum business. She became BP CEO in April 2026, the first woman to lead an international oil major. Her expansion strategy sits within debate over energy security and climate transition.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Participated in global energy-company operations and became the first female chief executive of an international oil major.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and upbringing
strings.facts.f1.value: Public birth records differ between 1970 and 1971; raised in Boulder, Colorado.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: MIT bachelor’s degrees in chemical and ocean engineering (1993); ocean systems management master’s (1994).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Engineering and global operations
strings.highlights.h1.text: Progressed from deepwater engineering analysis to production and leadership across countries.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Mergers and capital allocation
strings.highlights.h2.text: Led Woodside expansion through asset integration and long-term project investment.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Took office as BP CEO
strings.timeline.t1.text: Started on 1 April; current biography and first-day staff-note reporting confirm the transition.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Announced as BP successor
strings.timeline.t2.text: BP announced an appointment effective the following April; she had not yet taken office.
strings.timeline.t3.title: BHP petroleum merger completed

strings.timeline.t4.title: Permanent Woodside CEO
strings.timeline.t4.text: Moved from acting CEO to chief executive and managing director.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Became acting CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Peter Coleman while the board searched for a permanent leader.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joined Woodside
strings.timeline.t6.text: Moved from ExxonMobil and held operational leadership positions.
